q: GenXR-Bench: An open-source benchmark of 112 expert-authored tasks evaluating coding agents on XR software engineering, spanning SDK-level feature development, bug repair, and end-to-end application synthesis.
r: Include: new benchmark and test framework for coding agents including end-to-end application synthesis; contribution to evaluation method outweighs the XR domain limit.

q: We introduce evaluation-as-construction: rather than a static dataset, Trace2Eval is a periodically executable pipeline
r: Include: main contribution is a new trace-driven evaluation method with rubric scoring for coding agents on real user tasks.

q: Quality Assessment for AI Development tools (QAID), a comprehensive, vendorneutral meta-evaluation framework specifically designed for AI coding assistants.
r: Include: framework for evaluating and comparing AI coding assistants, a contribution to evaluation method.

q: In a within-subjects experiment of eight matched chatbot app microtasks with nine developers and 144 runs, the framework plus agent condition completed tasks 56 percent faster
r: Include: controlled within-subjects comparison of agent-only vs framework plus agent building apps, with time, cost and intervention metrics.

q: Since RACER is an autonomous bot, we propose addressing this challenge in two ways.
r: EC6: autonomous refactoring for maintenance at Meta; main contribution is the system and its production evaluation, not feature-level development or a general evaluation method.

q: We construct FullStack-Bench, a novel benchmark that comprehensively evaluates the functionalities of the generated full-stack websites.
r: Include: project-level full-stack website generation from requirements with a new benchmark, not only a new agent on an existing one.

q: first empirical study of 4bit weight-only quantization in execution-feedback coding agents.
r: EC6: tasks are competitive-programming problems (OJBench), function-level, not application development.
